eligible_questions.question: Under original Article 174 on 1 May 1950, which earlier clause qualified the Governor’s powers listed in clause (2)?
In original Article 174(2)(a), what words described the Governor’s discretion over the meeting time and place on 1 November 1950?
Under original Article 174(2)(c), what legislative body could the Governor dissolve on 1 February 1951?
Where did the original Article 174 place both its twice-yearly meeting requirement and its six-month interval rule on 16 June 1951?
On the first day the substituted Article 174 took effect, did clause (1) say the Governor “may” or “shall” summon the House or each House?
As of 1 April 2010, what two textual qualifications governed the Governor’s summons under Article 174(1)?
Under substituted Article 174(2)(b), applicable on 26 January 1960, which body is expressly named as the one the Governor may dissolve?
Compare original Article 174 with the replacement in force on 26 January 2020: where was the Governor’s summoning authority placed, and how did its operative verb change?
Comparing the original Article 174 with the substituted text applicable on 26 January 2000, which express yearly-frequency phrase was removed, and which inter-session safeguard remained?
In the original and substituted versions of Article 174, how did the stated object of the Governor’s prorogation power change?
